numerical_failure.observed_behavior: In scipy 1.14.0 scipy.special.pro_rad1(1,1,30,1.1) returns (-93126.77064342781, 2390688.1114633614) with no error or warning; the sphj translation from Fortran into C++ in specfun had argument-order and indexing errors (dj[0] written instead of dj[1] in sphj, and sphj called with swapped arguments in rmn1).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: pro_rad1(1,1,30,1.1) should return (0.009657798960703628, 3.253343602674869), matching scipy 1.11.4 and Mathematica (SpheroidalS1 0.00965787 and SpheroidalS1Prime 3.25337).
trigger_conditions: Calling scipy.special.pro_rad1 with parameters such as (1,1,30,1.1) on scipy 1.14.0
Code path through sphj in specfun.h, which pro_rad1 uses
Issue report says the wrong results appear for all input parameters tried
oracle_clues: Reference values from scipy 1.11.4 and Mathematica SpheroidalS1/SpheroidalS1Prime agree with each other
Commit adds a test for pro_rad1 and bumps test tolerance for linux 32bit, suggesting an assertNumerical-style tolerance comparison

numerical_characteristics.tolerance: rtol=2e-5 in the added test_pro_rad1 test; PR body states rtol 1e-5 for the added test; commit message mentions bumping test tolerance for linux 32bit (value not stated)
category_specific_evidence: Mathematica reference values: SpheroidalS1(1,1,30,1.1) = 0.00965787 and SpheroidalS1Prime(1,1,30,1.1) = 3.25337
Added test expects (0.009657872296166435, 3.253369651472877) for SpheroidalS1 and SpheroidalS1Prime with WolframAlpha as reference
Root cause: sphj in specfun was mistranslated from Fortran; dj[0] = 1.0/3.0 was changed to dj[1] = 1.0/3.0 because dj is zero-indexed in the Fortran as well
sphj is only used in pro_rad1; the existing pro_rad1 test did not cover the affected cases
Commit message: 'Fix indices in sphj' and 'Fix sphj argument order'
PR body: accuracy is now comparable to, slightly better than, the old Fortran implementation
reproduction_risks: Diff in specfun.h msta2 changes return nn to return nn + 10, an unexplained change that may affect results and should not be assumed part of the fix
The reproducer prints results without a dtype or tolerance specified; comparison depends on the rtol of 2e-5 and reference values from Mathematica/WolframAlpha, which are themselves rounded
Test tolerance was bumped for linux 32bit in a commit, value not given, so platform-dependent tolerance is unknown
